summary: This section requires a company to share certain member-requested resolutions and statements with its members. The company must receive a signed written request and enough money to cover costs within set time limits. The Central Government can stop the circulation of defamatory statements if the rights are abused.
points: The company must give notice to members about a proper resolution intended to be moved at a meeting when asked by the required number of members.
The company must circulate any statement about the proposed resolution or business to the members.
The signed request for a resolution must be deposited at the registered office at least six weeks before the meeting.
Any other request must be deposited at least two weeks before the meeting, and a sum for expenses must be deposited or tendered.
The company does not have to circulate a statement if the Central Government declares that the rights are being abused for needless defamatory publicity.
If the company fails to follow these rules, the company and any officer in default face a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees.
example: Asha and Rohan, members of Sunrise Garments Private Limited, want to propose a new resolution at their upcoming general meeting. They sign a written request and deposit it at the company's registered office, along with enough money to cover the mailing expenses, well within the time limit required by the law. They also want a supporting statement circulated to everyone. Sunrise Garments Private Limited must now give notice of this resolution and circulate their statement to all the members. If the company ignores this request and fails to comply, both the company and the responsible officers will be liable to pay a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees.

terms.meaning: A formal written request made by members to the company.
Harmful and false statements that damage someone's reputation.
The official main address of the company.

watch: A common confusion is thinking the company must pay for all the circulation costs itself, but the members must deposit or tender a sufficient sum for expenses.
